definition: Decorous means socially proper and dignified.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word decorous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know decorous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Applause at the chess final was decorous — a soft patter of fingertips, never a whoop.
Polite stops short of decorous — politeness covers small courtesies, while decorous conduct is a whole bearing of dignity.
Ceremonious goes further than decorous — every bow and greeting follows a full script of formal ritual.

Dignified describes a person's own bearing — calm, serious, worthy of respect — wherever they happen to be. Decorous measures conduct against the occasion instead: decorous behavior is whatever this particular ceremony or gathering calls for. A judge is dignified by temperament; her courtroom manners are decorous.

Seemly is an older word for behavior that looks right and proper to onlookers — nothing about it would raise an eyebrow. Decorous asks for more than the absence of anything unfitting: decorous conduct actively carries the dignity a particular occasion calls for.
